applies_why: The judge text makes an UNDERDETERMINED ruling and states its ground, so the rule governing grounds for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED applies.
quote: UNDERDETERMINED -- C4 pressed against the curse limb the defender dropped in [CR3] LINK 5, so no live link remains to contradict; the dropping is recorded there.
rule_words: That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand.
room: 'a single verse does not state a link or its contrary' — one reading forbids only explicitly using a single verse's failure to state a link or contrary as the ground; the other forbids any UNDERDETERMINED where a lone verse lacks a live opposing link. The judge relied on a dropped limb and no live link, not on a single verse's silence.
why: The judge's UNDERDETERMINED ground is that the defender dropped the curse limb, leaving no live link for C4 to contradict, not that a single verse fails to state a link or its contrary.
